newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-AUSTRALIA COLLAPSE ON OPENING DAY OF FIRST TEST.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-AUSTRALIA COLLAPSE ON OPENING DAY OF FIRST TEST.

text.p: Australia tumbled to 92 for eight on Thursday in one of the most remarkable collapses in test match history on the opening day of the first test against England.
England's pace bowlers Darren Gough, Devon Malcolm and Andy Caddick each found bounce and movement to share the wickets as sunshine gave way to cloud cover.
Mark Taylor's demons continued to haunt him when he was dismissed for only seven and his lack of confidence spread to to his team mates.
If winning the toss led Taylor to believe that his luck was changing, he was soon disillusioned.
After choosing to bat, he saw his opening partner Matthew Elliott bowled by Gough for six, then lost his own wicket when he edged a wide ball from Malcolm to new cap Mark Butcher at second slip.
This time he was not bailed out by his team mates.

When Gough, roared on by a noisy and enthusiastic sell-out crowd of 22,000, bowled Mark Waugh (five) and had Greg Blewett (seven) taken at third slip, Australia were 28 for four with less than an hour played.

As Gough rested, with figures of three for 18 in eight overs, New Zealand-born Caddick took over to send back Steve Waugh (12) and Ian Healy (0) in successive balls. Both were given out caught behind by Alec Stewart, though television replays suggested that Waugh had not touched the ball.
Michael Bevan (eight), the last recognised batsman, was next to go, giving Mark Ealham an easy catch at gully off Malcolm, who was returning to test cricket after an absence of 17 months.
Jason Gillespie, having narrowly avoided becoming a hat-trick victim, fell lbw in Caddick's next over for four.

Only Shane Warne resisted for long. Expected to be a potential match-winner with the ball rather than saviour with the bat, he took advantage of England's attacking fields to make 31 by lunch, when fellow tail-ender Mike Kasprowicz had made nine.
Their unbroken stand of 38 was by far the best of Australia's dismal innings to date.
